title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (section 8, 'le cas universel'). The groups are S = GL(2,Z)^ with S^+ = SL(2,Z), and S^{+^} = SL(2,Z)^ is the profinite completion of the oriented mapping class group T_{1,1}^+ of the once-punctured torus. Its centre is {±1}, and S^{+^}/{±1} is identified with S^^_{0,3} (profinite PSL(2,Z)). Pi^ is the level-2 congruence kernel, the inverse image of Pi^_{0,3}. M~_{0,3} is a group of automorphisms of the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus 3 points (a Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group). On the previous page Grothendieck builds a map (3), M~_{0,3} -> Aut(SL(2,Z)^), through the central extension 1 -> {±1} -> M -> M~_{0,3} -> 1. He shows (3) is injective because composing with Aut(SL2^) -> Aut(PSL2^) gives the canonical injection. He remarks that Aut(SL2^) -> Aut(PSL2^) is not injective: its kernel corresponds to homomorphisms SL2^ -> centre = {±1}.

On this page he computes that kernel.
- Such homomorphisms factor through the abelianisation. Using the presentation <rho, sigma | rho^6 = sigma^4 = 1, rho^3 = sigma^2>, the abelianisation is Z/12, with rho -> 2 and sigma -> 3.
- Hence the mod-2 abelianisation is Z/2, with rho -> 0 and sigma -> 1. There is exactly one nontrivial character sg: SL2^ -> {±1}.
- sg equals the composite SL2^ -> SL2^/Pi^ = SL(2,Z/2) = S_3 -> {±1}, i.e. the signature of a permutation.
- So the unique non-identity element of the kernel of (4) is Theta: x -> x·sg(x). It is an automorphism because sg(-1) = sg(sigma^2) = 1, and it is an involution.

He then sets L_0^S = eps_0^{Z^}, the inertia/cusp subgroup with eps_0 = sigma·rho (essentially ±T), and L_0^Pi = L_0^S ∩ Pi = l_0^{Z^} with l_0 = eps_0^2.
- Theta(eps_0) = -eps_0, since sg(eps_0) = -1.
- eps_0 is not conjugate to (-eps_0)^mu = -eps_0^mu for any mu in Z^*. Over SL(2,Z^) the traces are 2 versus -2.
- So Theta does not send L_0^S to a conjugate of itself, while Theta(l_0) = l_0 (next page).

Purpose: the next page's Proposition. The image of M~_{0,3} in Aut(SL(2,Z)^) consists exactly of the automorphisms u that (a) stabilise the level-2 kernel Pi^, and (b) send the cusp inertia eps_0 to a conjugate of eps_0^mu. Condition (b) is precisely what excludes the sign twist Theta. This is the 'universal case' of lifting GT/M_{0,3}-type automorphisms from profinite PSL2(Z) (equivalently pi_1 of M_{0,3}-type objects) to profinite SL2(Z) = pi_1(M_{1,1}).
errors: Minor: the notation (S^+_ab)_2 must mean S^+_ab ⊗ Z/2 (= Z/2), not the 2-primary part (which would be Z/4). The text is consistent with the former reading.
Minor: the presentation written includes the redundant relations [rho,sigma]=1 and rho^6=1 for the abelianisation; the result Z/12 with rho->2, sigma->3 is correct.
Implicit step: for x -> x·chi(x) to be an automorphism one needs chi(-1)=1. This holds here since -1 = sigma^2, but it is not stated.

ideas.what: Abelianisation of (profinite) SL(2,Z) is Z/12, with a unique nontrivial character to ±1 given by the sign of SL(2,Z/2) ≅ S_3
ideas.modern_name: Abelianisation of the modular group / sign character of SL2(F_2)

ideas.what: Kernel of Aut(SL2(Z)^) -> Aut(PSL2(Z)^) is {id, Theta}, with Theta the central twist x -> x·sg(x)
ideas.modern_name: Central automorphisms twisted by a character into the centre

ideas.what: Characterising lifts of GT-type automorphisms to profinite SL2(Z) = pi_1(M_{1,1}) by preserving the level-2 kernel and the conjugacy class of cusp inertia up to Z^*-power; the sign twist Theta is exactly what violates the inertia condition
ideas.modern_name: Action of GT^ on profinite SL2(Z)/B3 and preservation of inertia (genus 0 to genus 1 lifting)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the Teichmüller tower (M_{0,4}, M_{1,1}) qualitatively, not this lemma

missed.claim: Explicit observation that the only extra automorphism of SL2(Z)^ over PSL2(Z)^ is the sign twist, and that it fails to preserve cusp inertia (eps_0 -> -eps_0, trace 2 -> -2) while fixing l_0 = eps_0^2. This pins down M~_{0,3} inside Aut(SL2(Z)^). It is a careful but essentially standard detail of the later GT-on-M_{1,1} literature.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that Grothendieck worked out the genus-0 to genus-1 lifting (M_{0,3}/M_{0,4} vs M_{1,1}) at the level of automorphism groups. This matters historically for the GT literature, though mathematically it is not new.

deep.surprise_reason: Correct, careful but routine group-theoretic computation (abelianisation Z/12, sign character, central twist) serving a characterisation result that is close to known results on GT acting on profinite SL2(Z)/B3.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 likely reads 'on aura un seul homomorphisme [non trivial]' (completing the previous page's remark about Hom(S^+, ±1)).
'dans [?] ... [?] de (4)' should read 'dans le noyau de (4) est donné par' (the crossed '(3) est donné par' is replaced by '(4)').
The label above the arrow in (8) is 'sg' (the sign character), and the annotation under the arrow is 'signature d'une permutation'.
'que le sous-groupe Θ(L_0^S) ⊂ S^{+^} n'est pas S-conjugué à L_0, car :' — the crossed passage mentions Θ(L_0^Π) and 'il est engendré par Θ(ε_0)'.
Last line: '(car on voit' continues on the next page.
